newsitem.title: POLAND: PRESENT POLISH FISCAL,MONETARY TIGHT ENOUGH -BELKA.
newsitem.headline: PRESENT POLISH FISCAL,MONETARY TIGHT ENOUGH -BELKA.

text.p: Poland' present monetary policy and a planned cut in the 1998 budget deficit to below two percent of GDP should be tight enough to keep the trade deficit at safe levels, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.
Belka also told a news conference that the finance ministry would not seek to cap Poland's trade deficit by weakening the zloty.
"We have to cool internal demand and restrictive monetary and budget policies are needed...and I believe they should be as restrictive as they are now," Belka said.
"If it turns out that (present policies) are insufficient we will tighten them further, but it may prove unnecessary and I think that (what we have) will be sufficient," he added.

Belka said the $12 billion trade gap predicted for this year and the expected $6 billion current account deficit were at levels which posed no risk to Poland's stability and the current mix of monetary and fiscal measures should ensure that the trade gap does not get out of control next year.

Earlier this week the National Bank of Poland's deputy president said in a newspaper interview that unless the government balanced the budget next year the trade gap could soar to $16 billion -- a level which could threaten stability.

But Belka said the gradual monetary policy tightening, the present crawling peg devaluation of the zloty and the plan to cut budget deficit to below two percent from 2.8 percent, should start bearing fruit and help avoid problems next year.
"I think we want to see the effects of monetary policy adjustments too quickly," he said.

Belka said that even though balancing the budget was a desired longer-term target, achieving it next year was unrealistic and suggested that monetary adjustments would best serve to cool booming domestic demand and thus contain fast growing imports and trade gap.

"No one is really suggesting that we balance the budget next year, as anyone who knows the ramifications of the budget policy knows that it is inflexible and it is monetary policy which allowes more flexibility," he said.
